verdict.rationale: LangGraph's own docs describe stream/astream iterators with stream modes including messages, updates, tasks, custom and debug, plus per-projection event iterators, so token and intermediate-step streaming is a first-party capability. The evidence does not explicitly show tool-call events being streamed, and community reports say delivering the stream to a UI is a full implementation every client must build themselves, so coverage of the story is incomplete. missing for 10: explicit documentation of tool-call event streaming, a documented first-party path for delivering streams to a UI client, independent hands-on corroboration of real-time UI streaming.

support.subject: As a developer, I can stream tokens and intermediate agent events (tool calls, steps) to my UI in real time

citations.quote: LangGraph graphs expose the stream (sync) and astream (async) methods to yield streamed outputs as iterators.
It exposes graph execution through stream modes such as updates, values, messages, custom, checkpoints, tasks, and debug.
Event streaming gives you separate iterators per projection (messages, values, subgraphs, output) so you can consume them independently
